name.text: Forming inequalities for a computer laboratory layout

questiontext.text:
A computer laboratory space at Mtwapa Technical school in Mombasa restricts its layout based on two simple physical boundaries. Let \(x\) represent the horizontal floor width (in meters) and \(y\) represent the vertical floor length (in meters).

Examine the graphical layout below. Formulate the two linear inequalities that perfectly model the shaded permissible zone for computer placement.

[[jsxgraph width="600px" height="600px"]] var x_val = {#x_val#}; var y_val = {#y_val#}; var vert_solid = {#is_vert_solid_js#}; var horiz_solid = {#is_horiz_solid_js#}; var shade_right = {#is_shade_right_js#}; var shade_above = {#is_shade_above_js#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 12, -2], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); var xaxis = brd.create('axis', [[0, 0], [1, 0]], { name: 'x (Width in m)', withLabel: true, label: {position: 'rt', offset: [-45, 20]}, firstArrow: true, lastArrow: true, strokeWidth: 1.5, ticks: { drawLabels: true, label: {offset: [-8, -15]}, drawZero: true, insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 2, minorTicks: 1, majorHeight: -1, minorHeight: -1, strokeColor: '#a0a0a0', strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeWidth: 1, minorStrokeColor: '#e0e0e0', minorStrokeOpacity: 0.5, minorStrokeWidth: 1 } }); var yaxis = brd.create('axis', [[0, 0], [0, 1]], { name: 'y (Length in m)', withLabel: true, label: {position: 'rt', offset: [15, -15]}, firstArrow: true, lastArrow: true, strokeWidth: 1.5, ticks: { drawLabels: true, label: {offset: [-25, -5]}, drawZero: false, insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 2, minorTicks: 1, majorHeight: -1, minorHeight: -1, strokeColor: '#a0a0a0', strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeWidth: 1, minorStrokeColor: '#e0e0e0', minorStrokeOpacity: 0.5, minorStrokeWidth: 1 } }); /* Draw the vertical boundary line */ var v_line = brd.create('line', [[x_val, 0], [x_val, 1]], { strokeWidth: 3, strokeColor: '#1565c0', dash: vert_solid ? 0 : 2, highlight: false }); /* Draw the horizontal boundary line */ var h_line = brd.create('line', [[0, y_val], [1, y_val]], { strokeWidth: 3, strokeColor: '#c62828', dash: horiz_solid ? 0 : 2, highlight: false }); /* Shade the permissible intersection zone */ var px = shade_right ? 15 : -5; var py = shade_above ? 15 : -5; brd.create('polygon', [[x_val, y_val], [px, y_val], [px, py], [x_val, py]], { fillColor: '#673ab7', fillOpacity: 0.15, borders: {strokeWidth: 0} }); /* Explicitly label the equations of the lines as shown in the textbook */ brd.create('text', [x_val + 0.3, 10, 'x = ' + x_val], {fontSize: 16, strokeColor: '#1565c0'}); brd.create('text', [10, y_val + 0.4, 'y = ' + y_val], {fontSize: 16, strokeColor: '#c62828'}); [[/jsxgraph]]

Analyze the line styles and shading directions to write the two independent inequalities.

Vertical boundary constraint (\(x\)): [[input:ans1]]

Horizontal boundary constraint (\(y\)): [[input:ans2]]

Vertical constraint check: [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
Horizontal constraint check: [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

By analyzing the geometric boundaries independently:

1. The Vertical Boundary
The vertical blue line is plotted exactly at \( x = {@x_val@} \).
It is drawn as a {@v_style@} line, and the shaded permissible zone lies to the {@v_shade@} of this line. This indicates that the valid \(x\)-values are strictly {@v_val_str@} than the boundary.
Therefore, the vertical constraint is:
\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@ta1@}} \)

2. The Horizontal Boundary
The horizontal red line is plotted exactly at \( y = {@y_val@} \).
It is drawn as a {@h_style@} line, and the shaded permissible zone lies {@h_shade@} this line. This indicates that the valid \(y\)-values are {@h_val_str@} than the boundary.
Therefore, the horizontal constraint is:
\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@ta2@}} \)

The combined system of linear inequalities defining the computer lab layout is \( {@ta1@} \) and \( {@ta2@} \).
